question: Did the batteries destroy German aircraft at 1500 on 12 January?
claim: No German record read reports a German aircraft lost that day
source: XIV Panzer Corps' reports of 12.1.1944 (army records: they report the enemy's air attacks and their own Flak's successes, not the Luftwaffe's losses)
note: Silence in an army corps' reports is weak evidence: the Luftwaffe's losses were reported in its own channels.

question: Did the batteries destroy German aircraft at 1500 on 12 January?
claim: Two loss lists for II./SG 4 (the Fw 190 fighter-bomber Gruppe then flying over this front) have no loss on 12 January; one aircraft "destroyed without enemy action on an operational flight" on the 11th and another on the 13th
source: Forum posts by L. Rizzotti and B. Lander, 12 O'Clock High, thread 18830 (2009), compiled from the Luftwaffe's loss returns (secondary; the two may share a source, so they count once)
note: Not the loss returns themselves (BA-MA RL 2 III), which are not seen. A damaged aircraft that got home would not be a loss. The Kracker Luftwaffe Archive, also built from the returns, put up a bot check.

question: Which German unit made the 1500 raid?
claim: II./SG 4 flew Fw 190 fighter-bombers over this front and lost aircraft to anti-aircraft fire here before: "10/11/43 Lt. ... KIA Fw.190G-3 (160052) Venafro A/A Fire"; "03/01/44 ... Fw190G-3 (160020) S.Elia A/A"
source: B. Lander's list of II./SG 4 casualties, 12 O'Clock High thread 18830 (secondary)
note: For: Battery G saw dive-bombing Fw 190s. Against: no German record places II./SG 4 over Filignano on 12 January. Battery F saw Me 109s, which would fit an escort or a Bf 109 Jabo unit.
